name: Calibrated Math (Lin et al.)
why_it_matters: Reporters and readers need to know when a model is guessing; calibration benchmarks test whether stated confidence tracks actual accuracy.
task_shape: Models answer arithmetic/word problems and must express confidence in words or numbers; scores compare stated confidence against correctness using calibration metrics like expected calibration error and Brier score.
signals: Directly measures whether verbalized confidence is trustworthy, which maps to newsroom needs for hedged answers.
Narrow math domain limits generalization to open-ended journalism queries about sources, quotes, or documents.

source.label: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words (arXiv:2205.14334)
